Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

event noun

something that happens

also happening, occurrence, events, incident, incidents

classical

Cic. Att. 1.13.2: rēs dignae litterīs nostrīs

rēs, reī f.

noun, fifth declension

a thing that happens, an event, an affair

Lewis & Short: a matter, affair, event, fact, occurrence. What happened is also said with a clause, quod accidit, quid reliquīs acciderit (Caes. BC 1.21). For an organised event Latin names the occasion: convīvium, spectāculum, lūdī.

Other words

  • rēs gestae, rērum gestārum f. pl. — events, what was done; deeds

    noun, fifth declension, plural, with a participle · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. gerō

  • cāsus, cāsūs m. — a chance event, an accident, a misfortune

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.15: quid cāsus, quid ēventus (Lewis & Short)

  • ēventus, ēventūs m. — an occurrence; far more often, the outcome

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.63: cōnsilia prīmum, deinde ācta, posteā ēventūs exspectantur (Lewis & Short)

    Rare in the sense of an event; usually the result of an action (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • sunt autem post discessum ā mē tuum rēs dignae litterīs nostrīs

    since you left me there have been events worth a letterCic. Att. 1.13.2

See also what happened?, history, happen.
